notes:
ROUND 56 - bank-page / hiring-firm career reading. 5 records filed; 4 name a private financial employer.

PRIORITY 1 RESULTS
COLOMBIA - CLOSED (private). Searched former Banco de la Republica board members against private Colombian financial groups rather than re-reading the bank's own biographies (which earlier rounds showed are entirely public/multilateral). La Republica (27 Jun 2024) reports Gerardo Hernandez Correa spent 16 years at Banco de la Republica, including as codirector (board member), executive manager and secretary of the Board, then six years as Superintendente Financiero, then from 2021 vice-president of legal affairs at Banco de Bogota, and in June 2024 was named president of Banco AV Villas. The same article states Grupo Aval holds controlling stakes in financial entities including Banco AV Villas. Grupo Aval is a private financial conglomerate, not a state body. Filed.
GUYANA - CLOSED (private). The hiring-firm route worked. Demerara Bank Limited publishes PER-PERSON director profile pages (demerarabank.com/team/<name>/), not just the board listing page that earlier rounds read. The profile of director Mr. Rajendra Rampersaud states he "served as Director at the Bank of Guyana until 2018" with "over two decades of central banking experience". Ownership fact comes from Demerara Bank's own audited Annual Report 2023 (note 1, Incorporation and business activities): "Demerara Bank Limited was incorporated on January 20, 1992 as a private limited liability company under the provisions of the Companies Act, Chapter 89:01". Private, in finance. Filed.
SOUTH KOREA - STILL HELD for the ownership fact. Year is now established: the appointment of Jeong Gyu-il as CEO/President of Seoul Foreign Exchange Brokerage (Seoul Money Brokerage Services, Ltd) was made at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting reported by Asiae on 2 July 2021 (https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2021070215182015950); the same article confirms he joined the Bank of Korea in 1987 and held Deputy Director of the Economic Research Institute, Director of International Cooperation, Director of Economic Statistics and Deputy Governor. The article does NOT name the company's shareholders. The Bank of Korea's own FX market page (https://www.bok.or.kr/eng/main/contents.do?menuNo=400184) lists Seoul Money Brokerage Services, Ltd first among ten authorised foreign exchange brokerage companies and says a brokerage needs authorisation from the Ministry of Strategy and Finance - but it says NOTHING about who owns it, and silence is not evidence of private ownership. The company's own site (smbs.biz) would not resolve through the proxy (connection failed, HTTP 000). A Korean-language search for its shareholder list returned nothing on point. For comparison, the rival brokerage Korea Money Brokerage Corp publishes its own ownership on https://kmbco.com/eng/introduce/company.do - 47 institutions: 17 commercial banks 39%, KR&C (state resolution company) 22.1%, 19 securities companies 21%, 2 insurers 4%, 7 others 1.4% - i.e. the comparable Korean money brokerage is MIXED, with a state entity holding 22%. That makes it unsafe to assume Seoul Money Brokerage is wholly private. NOT FILED. What would close it: a shareholder list on smbs.biz, a DART/FSS filing, or a Korean business-registry extract for 서울외국환중개.
NORTH MACEDONIA - STILL NOT FILABLE. The NBRSM CV search surfaced only the same Fadil Bajrami CV page (https://nbrm.mk/ns-newsarticle-cv_fadil_bajrami.nspx) that withholds the firm and the industry. No other source named the employer. A private move not shown to be financial must not be counted, so nothing filed.
MOZAMBIQUE - still blank, and the two new leads both failed. (1) Banco de Mocambique's own published CV of board member Gertrudes A. Macueve Tovela (https://www.bancomoc.mz/media/pwhfq0cm/curriculum-vitae-gertrudes-tovela.pdf) gives a full dated career but every outside employer is public: Deputy National Director for Infrastructure and Information Systems at the Ministry of Science and Technology 2010-2015, lecturer at Universidade Eduardo Mondlane since 2001, and systems analyst/software developer at Empresa Portos e Caminhos de Ferro de Mocambique (the state ports and railways company) 2000-2004. No private financial employer, so not filed. (2) The hiring-firm route via Standard Bank Mocambique failed: the Forbes Africa Lusofona announcement of Esselina Macome as Chair of the Board from 1 December 2022 (https://forbesafricalusofona.com/?p=49633) lists her as associate professor at UEM, Executive Director of FSDMoc and previously non-executive director of Standard Bank - it mentions NO role at the central bank.
SIERRA LEONE, ZAMBIA - no new route found within budget; not re-attempted beyond one search each that returned only the bank's own board page and parliamentary approval notices already known to give appointment dates only.

PRIORITY 2 RESULTS
ALBANIA - FILED (private). The Bank of Albania publishes a long narrative biography of Governor Gent Sejko on its Supervisory Council page naming the private banks by name. Ownership of Societe Generale confirmed from Societe Generale's own investor-relations capital breakdown page (31 Dec 2025): free float 72.72%, employee shareholding 9.11%, asset managers 14.39% (BlackRock 7.93%, Amundi 2.70%, Capital Group 2.33%, BNPP AM 1.43%), treasury 1.57%, and one public financial institution, Caisse des Depots et Consignations, at 2.22%; no French State stake is listed. Mixed ownership is stated on the face of the record.
GEORGIA - FILED (private, mixed). The National Bank of Georgia publishes per-person board profile pages with fully dated work-experience lists. Vice-Governor Nino Jeladze's page gives an 18-year career at ProCredit. Ownership from ProCredit Holding's own shareholder-structure page, whose footnotes name Zeitinger Invest GmbH, Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW, the German state development bank), DOEN Participaties and the EBRD - a privately listed German group with state-development and multilateral shareholders, i.e. mixed. Stated on the face of the record.
  Also read but NOT filed: board member Levan Dzneladze's page (https://nbg.gov.ge/en/about-us/board-members/levan-dznelad-1) gives a full dated career with 2009-2011 JSC Deputy General Director / Financial Director at Cartu Group, 2006-2009 General Director at GMC Group and 2002-2006 General Director at Imedi Media Group. Cartu Group's ownership and whether it is a financial business are not characterised by the page, and GMC/Imedi are not finance, so this is held for want of an ownership-and-sector fact. Vice-Governor pages for Ekaterine Galdava, Ekaterine Mikabadze, Natia Turnava and Robert H. Singleton were not read within budget and are a good next target - the per-person format is reliable.
MOLDOVA - FILED, with a caveat the map owner should decide on. The National Bank of Moldova publishes print-friendly per-person pages. Deputy Governor Constantin Schendra's page gives a fully dated career: senior auditor at Ernst & Young Moldova 2010-2015 and Ernst & Young Cyprus 2013-2014, executive director at Baker Tilly Moldova 2015-2018, then Director of the NBM Banking Supervision Department 2018-2021 and Deputy Governor from 4 November 2021. The bank's own page characterises these as "international audit companies" and credits him with "over 8 years in international audit companies". CAVEAT: these are private professional audit and advisory firms, not banks, insurers or investors; the page does not state their ownership (they are private partnerships, with no state body involved). If the map counts only banks/insurers/brokers/funds and not financial-services consultancies, drop this one.
  Also read, NOT filed: First Deputy Governor Petru Rotaru's page (https://bnm.md/en/print/content/petru-rotaru-first-deputy-governor-national-bank-moldova) says that from 2006 to 2016 he held "managerial roles in both private and public sector entities" in accounting and administration but names no firm and no industry - a private move not shown to be financial, so not counted. His other posts (Court of Accounts, State Tax Service, Minister of Finance) are all public. The page for First Deputy Governor Vladimir Munteanu returned HTTP 403 "You are not authorized to access this page" through the proxy.
MONTENEGRO - HELD FOR AN OWNERSHIP FACT. The Central Bank of Montenegro publishes dated per-person vice-governor pages. Gordana Kalezic's page (https://www.cbcg.me/en/vicegovernors/gordana-kalezic) states she has been Vice-Governor since 2025, was at the CBCG 2019-2025, and from 2016 to 2019 was Director of the Unit for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing at AZMONT BANK AD PODGORICA, a commercial bank - before that, 2007-2016 at the state Administration for the Prevention of Money Laundering. That is a clean bank-to-central-bank move, but Azmont Bank's ownership is exactly the Zambia trap. SEENews reports Azmont Investment, which launched the bank, is "a subsidiary of Azerbaijan Global Investments (AGI)", described as "a consortium of three leading Azerbaijani Investment Holding companies", and notes Azmont's PREVIOUS parent was SOCAR, the State Oil Company of the Azerbaijan Republic (https://seenews.com/news/azerbaijan-owned-azmont-investment-launches-banking-operations-in-montenegro-528935). The article does not classify AGI or its three holding companies as private or state-owned. With a state oil company in the chain of title and no statement of AGI's ownership, this cannot be filed. What would close it: the ownership section of Azmont Banka's or Nova Banka's own licence disclosure, a CBCG shareholder disclosure for the bank, or the Montenegrin central company registry (CRPS) entry for Azmont Banka AD Podgorica. (The bank was later renamed Nova Banka and then bought by US-based Adriatic Capital, per SEENews, but that is after her tenure.)
  Also read, nothing filed: Vice-Governor Zorica Kalezic (IMF and World Bank constituency advisory roles only - all public), Vice-Governor Milan Remikovic (entire career inside the CBCG), and Governor Irena Radovic (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, British Council, ambassadorial and UNESCO posts - all public).
DOMINICAN REPUBLIC, CAMBODIA - one search each returned no published career list naming a private financial employer; the DR coverage is dominated by Governor Valdez Albizu's 50 years inside the Banco Central, and Cambodia's by Governor Chea Serey's career inside the NBC. Not spent further.
BOLIVIA, ECUADOR, GAMBIA, NICARAGUA, LAOS, MYANMAR, BRUNEI, TONGA, ARMENIA, AZERBAIJAN, KYRGYZSTAN, SERBIA, TUNISIA, UZBEKISTAN - not reached within budget, no calls spent on most. Serbia's management page (https://nbs.rs/en/o_nbs/rukovodstvo/) and Armenia's hiring-firm route (Ameriabank and ACBA both publish per-person PDF board biographies at acba.am/files/<Name>-eng.pdf and ameriabank.am/investors/ESG/Governance/...) are the strongest untried leads for a next round.

records.people: Gent Sejko (Governor and Chairman of the Supervisory Council)
records.move: from Deputy General Manager of Societe Generale Albania to Governor of the Bank of Albania (5 February 2015), after senior executive and committee-chairing roles at the National Commercial Bank, the American Bank of Albania and Raiffeisen Bank
records.summary: The Bank of Albania's own biography page for Gent Sejko states he has been Governor and Chairman of the Supervisory Council since 5 February 2015, was re-elected for a second term on 24 February 2022, and that prior to his appointment as Governor he served as Deputy General Manager of Societe Generale Albania, having earlier held senior executive positions and chaired committees at the National Commercial Bank, the American Bank of Albania and Raiffeisen Bank, with responsibilities spanning corporate and retail banking, audit and compliance, and leasing; Societe Generale is a private commercial and investment bank in finance, and its own investor-relations capital breakdown as of 31 December 2025 shows 72.72% free float, 9.11% employee shareholding, 14.39% held by asset managers (BlackRock 7.93%, Amundi 2.70%, Capital Group 2.33%, BNPP AM 1.43%), 1.57% treasury and one public financial institution, Caisse des Depots et Consignations, at 2.22%, with no French State stake listed, so ownership is predominantly private with a small public minority - that ownership fact comes from investors.societegenerale.com, not from the Bank of Albania page, which only calls the employers the commercial banking sector.
records.source_title: Mr. Gent Sejko, Governor of the Bank of Albania

records.people: Nino Jeladze (Vice-Governor and member of the Board)
records.move: from JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia and ProCredit Holding (Frankfurt) to the National Bank of Georgia, where she became Head of the Supervisory Policy Department in 2024 and Vice-Governor on 10 February 2025
records.summary: The National Bank of Georgia's own board-member profile page for Nino Jeladze gives a fully dated career: account manager at JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia in 2003, head of its customer service department 2004-2005, branch manager including of the central branch 2006-2014, operational risk manager 2014-2015, operational risk manager at ProCredit Holding in Frankfurt 2015-2017, head of anti-money laundering and compliance at JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia 2017-2021, consultant in private practice 2022-2023, then head of the NBG's Supervisory Policy Department 2024-2025 and Vice-Governor and board member since 10 February 2025 for a term to February 2032; the employer is a commercial bank and so is in finance, and its ownership is mixed rather than state - ProCredit Holding's own shareholder-structure page names Zeitinger Invest GmbH, Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW, the German state development bank), DOEN Participaties and the EBRD as the reporting shareholders of the listed German group, so the ownership fact comes from procredit-holding.com and is stated here as mixed private, state-development and multilateral.
records.source_title: Nino Jeladze - Member of the Board of the National Bank of Georgia, Vice-Governor

records.people: Rajendra Rampersaud (Director at the Bank of Guyana)
records.move: from Director at the Bank of Guyana (until 2018) to Director of Demerara Bank Limited
records.summary: Demerara Bank Limited's own director profile page for Mr. Rajendra Rampersaud, published on its board-members listing dated 21 September 2022, states that he has over two decades of central banking experience and served as Director at the Bank of Guyana until 2018, holds master's degrees in monetary economics and finance from the University of Glasgow and in economics and planning from Moscow, and has contributed to the Inter-American Development Bank and the Caribbean Development Bank, and it lists him as a Director of the bank; the hiring employer is in finance and is private, and that ownership fact comes from Demerara Bank Limited's own audited Annual Report 2023, note 1 Incorporation and business activities, which states that the bank was incorporated on 20 January 1992 as a private limited liability company under the Companies Act Chapter 89:01 and was licensed to carry on the business of banking on 31 October 1994.
records.source_title: Mr. Rajendra Rampersaud, Director - Demerara Bank Limited

records.people: Gerardo Hernandez Correa (codirector of the Banco de la Republica, executive manager and secretary of its Board)
records.move: from codirector, executive manager and secretary of the Board of the Banco de la Republica to vice-president of legal affairs at Banco de Bogota from 2021 ; to president of Banco AV Villas, announced 27 June 2024
records.summary: La Republica's report of 27 June 2024 states that Gerardo Hernandez Correa will become president of Banco AV Villas, replacing Juan Camilo Angel, that he spent sixteen years at the Banco de la Republica in roles including codirector (board member), executive manager and secretary of the Board, that he was Superintendente Financiero of Colombia for six years, and that immediately before the AV Villas appointment he had been vice-president of legal affairs at Banco de Bogota since 2021; both hiring employers are commercial banks and so are in finance, and both are private rather than state - the same article states that Grupo Aval holds controlling stakes in financial entities including Banco AV Villas, and Grupo Aval is a private financial conglomerate and not a state body, so the ownership fact comes from this article and not from any Banco de la Republica page.
records.source_title: Gerardo Hernandez sera el presidente del Banco AV Villas

records.people: Constantin Schendra (Deputy Governor and member of the Executive Committee)
records.move: from senior auditor at Ernst & Young Moldova (2010-2015) and Ernst & Young Cyprus (2013-2014) and executive director at Baker Tilly Moldova (2015-2018) to Director of the Banking Supervision Department of the National Bank of Moldova (2018-2021) and then Deputy Governor (4 November 2021)
records.summary: The National Bank of Moldova's own biography page for Constantin Schendra states that he was appointed Deputy Governor and member of the Executive Committee by Parliament decision no. 161 of 4 November 2021, that at the time of his appointment he had over 18 years of experience in the economic and banking sector including over eight years in international audit companies, and gives the dated sequence: accountant at the Center for Economic and Social Development from 2002, grant financial manager at Citizen Network for Foreign Affairs in 2005, regional director of the USAID Community Connections programme 2005-2010, senior auditor at Ernst & Young Moldova 2010-2015 and at Ernst & Young Cyprus 2013-2014, executive director at Baker Tilly Moldova 2015-2018, and Director of the NBM Banking Supervision Department 2018-2021; Ernst & Young and Baker Tilly are private firms and no state body is involved in them, but the page does not state their ownership and they are audit and advisory practices in financial services rather than banks, insurers, brokerages or funds, so the sector characterisation here rests on the National Bank's own words international audit companies and the map owner should judge whether a financial-services consultancy counts.
records.source_title: Mr. Constantin Schendra, Deputy Governor of the NBM
